contentBlocks.body:
**Objective.** Prevent stale edits from overwriting newer work and stop simultaneous last-unit reservations from overselling.

This is a real project lab in projects/inventory-desk, also available from the Projects page as a source download. Work in an isolated copy of the reference project so you can compare your change with a known baseline. Read InventoryDesk.Api/Program.cs; InventoryDesk.Api/DeskDb.cs before editing. Trace one request from the UI or test through the boundary that owns the behavior.

**Acceptance criteria.** A stale version returns 409 without overwriting; two concurrent reservations of the last unit produce one success, one conflict, and stock zero.

**Make a meaningful variation.** Show the latest product next to the user's unsaved edit when a conflict occurs. Require an explicit choice before replacing either version. Write the observable expectation before editing the implementation. If the variation exposes a defect, keep the smallest failing fixture as a regression test.
Review rubric: The version and stock predicates participate in the database write; a preliminary read is not the only safeguard.

**Explain the boundary.** Where must the final stock condition be evaluated? Describe both a successful case and a rejected or missing-data case. Compare actual output with the acceptance criteria, including status codes, persisted values, and user-visible feedback where relevant.

**Evidence to keep.** Save the focused test result, a short before/after diff, and a note explaining one tradeoff. Completing the quiz records this lesson's concepts; it does not run the companion checks or certify that the project milestone is finished.
